chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Maymun, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him: 'If a man prays behind us and we follow him, is he more beloved to you [to follow] or [is it better] in the mosque?' He said: 'The mosque is more beloved to me.'
ai.seo_question: Is it better to follow a specific imam or pray in the mosque?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the merit of the physical space and the status of the leader, affirming that the sanctity of the mosque itself holds greater preference than merely following a specific individual. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the communal and spatial dimensions of worship, where the mosque serves as a focal point for unity and divine presence, independent of the specific identity of the imam leading the prayer.
